question: Is the parastatal mandated to prepare its spatial and/or sectoral plans in coordination with the ULG(s) within its jurisdiction?
step2_answer: ANSWER: Not determined. No provision in the Citation Sheet requires BWSSB to prepare its spatial or sectoral plans in coordination with, or with approval from, the GBA or the City Corporations. The only nearby mechanisms are advisory or run in the opposite direction. | EVIDENCE: (1) BWSSB Act 1964 s.14 (FAOLEX copy, as amended). The State Government 'shall constitute a Consultative Committee'. Its members are Board members plus 3-9 others appointed 'after consultation with' bodies representing the Municipal Corporation of the City of Bangalore, the Bangalore City Improvement Trust Board and water consumers. Its function is 'to advise the Board on major questions of policy and major schemes'. This is an advisory body, and ULG input only shapes who is appointed. It is not mandatory ULG consultation on plan preparation. The Act names the old Corporation, and no official source in the sheet shows the GBA substituted. (2) BWSSB Act s.36 and s.38 cover water supply to the Corporation and public hydrants. They do not deal with plan preparation. (3) Greater Bengaluru Governance Act 2024 (Gazette text as published 24.04.2025), s.14(2)(a): the GBA 'shall be the Planning Authority' under the Karnataka T&CP Act 1961 for the Greater Bengaluru Area. Section 15(5) says the GBA 'may assign the task of planning the major infrastructural projects' to public authorities and that 'The agencies shall be bound to assist the Greater Bengaluru Authority when called up on to do so.' This is a GBA-to-
quote: to advise the Board on major questions of policy and major schemes;

Evidence read: BWSSB Act s.14 (Consultative Committee) and s.15 (general duties). Section 14 is advisory. The State Government forms the committee, and the Municipal Corporation of the City of Bangalore and the BCITB are only consulted on who is appointed. Section 15(2)(b)-(c) says the Board prepares schemes, and schemes costing over Rs 1 crore need State Government approval. No ULG coordination, consultation or approval is required for plan preparation. The Step 2 answer also found no such duty in the Greater Bengaluru Governance Act 2024 s.14-15, where 'may assign' is discretionary and runs from the GBA to the agency. It found none in the T&CP Act 1961 either. The 0 band is not entered for three reasons. First, the BWSSB Act copy is a FAOLEX mirror, which is blocked and serves only as a lead. Second, no BWSSB Rules or Regulations are in the sheet. Third, the full text of the Governance Act was not read in full. This is not affirmative absence. A person should check an official copy of the BWSSB Act, the BWSSB Rules and Regulations, and the whole of the Governance Act, including any substitution of the GBA for the Corporation named in s.14. The likely outcome is 0, or at most 2.5 if the advisory committee is read as discretionary consultation. Confidence is low.

question: Is the parastatal mandated to prepare its spatial and/or sectoral plans in coordination with the ULG(s) within its jurisdiction?
step2_answer: ANSWER: Not determined. In the excerpts read, no provision requires BDA to prepare its master plan or other plans in coordination with the GBA or the City Corporations. The only ULG-specific mechanism found (concurrence of the Corporation, with disputes referred to Government) covers sanction of layouts proposed by other persons, not BDA's own plans. The nearest band is 0 (no formal role), but a 0 needs affirmative absence, which I could not establish. The GBA Act also appears to make the GBA the 'Planning Authority' for the Greater Bengaluru Area, so BDA's planning role needs team clarification. | EVIDENCE: (1) BDA Act 1976, s.32(1) provisos: no extension or layout within the local limits of the Corporation may be sanctioned by BDA 'without the concurrence of the Corporation'; disagreement goes to Government, whose decision is final. This governs sanction of layouts formed by 'any person', so it is a partial-scope concurrence mechanism for layouts, not for BDA's own master plan. BDA Act s.30(3) refers Authority-Corporation disputes on street and open-space transfer to Government. BDA Act s.67 inserted s.81-B in the T&CP Act, making BDA the local Planning Authority for the Bangalore local planning area. provision: BDA Act 1976 s.32(1) provisos; s.25(1) proviso; s.15(2)(ii)

What the BDA Act shows:
- s.32(1) requires the Corporation's concurrence, but only for layouts that other persons propose within Corporation limits. It does not cover BDA's own master plan or sectoral plans. Disagreements go to Government, whose decision is final.
- s.25(1) proviso says 'the Corporation shall be consulted' when BDA takes up works for further development of an area within the City of Bangalore. This is a mandatory 'shall' consultation. It covers works, not plans, and it sits under a Government-sanction power. Step 2 missed this provision. If works count as sectoral plans, it would fit the 5-band of the methodology (5 of 10, i.e. 2.5 of 5): consultation is mandatory with no duty to respond. That is a judgement for a person to make.
- s.15(2)(ii) lets BDA take up development schemes on the Corporation's recommendation, but only if the local authority provides the funds. It is not a coordination mandate.
- ss.16-19 on the procedure for development schemes were not read in full.

What the T&CP Act shows: ss.9-10 provide public notice and consideration of suggestions, which is not ULG consultation. I found no provision requiring consultation with the ULG. s.13 was only partly seen.

What is unresolved:
- BDA Act s.67 inserted s.81-B into the T&CP Act, making BDA the Planning Authority. The GBA Act 2024 (Act 36 of 2025) also names the GBA as 'Planning Authority' for the Greater Bengaluru Area. Neither source shows how the two interact. They also don't show whether the GBA or City Corporations are substituted for 'Corporation'.
- Rules and regulations under both Acts are not in the Citation Sheet.

I found no ULG approval, concurrence, joint preparation or mandatory consultation. Absence is not affirmed, because the full T&CP Act text and the Rules were not read. The section has no consultation or ULG-approval requirement. s.9(1)(ix) is a function 'to co-ordinate the activities of the Bangalore Development Authority, the Corporation of the City of Bangalore, ...'. That is BMRDA coordinating other bodies' activities, not a duty to plan with the ULG. s.10 requires other authorities to get BMRDA permission for specified developments, which runs from the ULG to BMRDA. The Act's text is on an unofficial host (India Water Portal). T&CP Act s.81-C (inserted by the BMRDA Act s.31): Planning Authorities in the region submit their plans to the State Government 'through' BMRDA for approval, and BMRDA exercises the Director of Town Planning's powers.
